audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage was keyed to Demonic Ascension, a 120s ultimate, instead of Nevermove — the 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s root that actually decides each trade.
audit.why: You cannot trade 'around' a 120-second cooldown; the lane is played on the E timer.
audit.corrected: Cooldown and phase text now name Nevermove at 12s rank 1 as the tracked cooldown.

audit.why: Spikes already track level 6 and first item correctly, and level 6 belonging to Swain matches Demonic Ascension coming online.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text claimed Twilight Shroud makes you untargetable so 'his E can't pin you', and never mentioned Vision of Empire revealing you.
audit.why: Nevermove is a skillshot wave that roots enemies it hits — unselectable does not stop it, and Riot flags Vision of Empire as revealing champions hit, which strips your shroud invisibility outright. Also the root is on the wave's RETURN, not the outgoing cast.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the shroud lines: the smoke denies him the aim, not the wave; Vision of Empire reveals you inside it; sidestep the return claw, which is the half that roots.

edits.before: Respect Swain's E (Nevermove) — it's a slow, telegraphed double-claw root, but if it lands he free-casts Q's cone and W's damage zone on you before you have Shroud to escape, and that's his only kill threat pre-6.
edits.after: Respect Swain's E (Nevermove) — the outgoing claw does nothing, it is the RETURN wave that roots, so sidestep on the way back. If it lands he free-casts Q's cone and W's zone on you, and it is his only kill threat pre-6.

edits.before: Twilight Shroud (W) goes online: drop smoke and you can sidestep his E root from invisibility, so his W zone and Q cone whiff while your passive ring-autos chip him down.
edits.after: Twilight Shroud (W) goes online, but smoke denies him the aim, not the wave — Nevermove roots straight through it, and Vision of Empire reveals you inside the shroud.

edits.before: Sit in Twilight Shroud to go untargetable so his E can't pin you for the free Q-cone and W-zone follow-up
edits.after: Shroud breaks his aim, then keep moving — Nevermove roots through smoke and Vision of Empire reveals you

edits.before: Land E (Nevermove) to root you in place, then free-cast Q's cone and stack W's zone for a no-counterplay trade
edits.after: Land the RETURN half of E (Nevermove) to root you, then free-cast Q's cone and stack W's zone for a no-counterplay trade

edits.before: Levels 1-3 lean Swain because his root sets up everything, but it's a skillshot, not point-and-click — E (Nevermove) is a slow, telegraphed double claw, and if you eat it he free-casts Q's bolt cone and drops W's damage zone on you while you have no Shroud to escape. Don't walk into the wave to last-hit with Q; take CS at the tip of your Five Point Strike range and never give him a clean E angle. His Q cone chips and his W zones your approach, but he has no kill pressure until that root lands, so the whole early game is just sidestepping it.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 lean Swain because his root sets up everything, but it's a skillshot, not point-and-click — E (Nevermove) throws a claw out and roots only on the return, so watch the way back, not the way out. Eat it and he free-casts Q's bolt cone and drops W's damage zone while you have no Shroud. Don't walk into the wave to last-hit with Q; take CS at the tip of your Five Point Strike range and never give him a clean E angle. He has no kill pressure until that root lands, so the early game is sidestepping it — 12s at rank 1.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to me. Once W (Twilight Shroud) is up around 4-5 I sit in the smoke and go untargetable, so I can sidestep his E from inside it — and if his root can't pin me, his Q cone and W zone are just wasted mana. I bait the E, let it whiff, then E-flip in and Q-sweetspot for a real trade, healing off my passive ring. At 6 my R is the payoff: dodge the Nevermove, flip onto him, and Perfect Execution's second cast executes on his missing health before his Demonic Ascension drain heals it back. The one rule is never all-in while his E is up — eat one root and he gets the whole combo for free.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Once W (Twilight Shroud) is up around 4-5 the smoke denies him the aim — but it does not blank the wave, Nevermove roots straight through it, and Vision of Empire reveals you inside it, so keep moving rather than sitting still. Bait the E, let the return claw whiff, then E-flip in and Q-sweetspot for a real trade, healing off your passive ring. At 6 your R is the payoff: dodge the Nevermove, flip onto him, and Perfect Execution's second cast executes his missing health before Demonic Ascension drains it back. The one rule is never all-in while his E is up — 12s at rank 1.

edits.before: I still win the straight 1v1, but Swain is a soul-stacking scaler — full-AP with Liandry's and Rylai's, his R (Demonic Ascension) becomes a near-permanent AoE drain and Rylai's slow makes him sticky enough to land E mid-fight. If I let it go long he out-sustains my burst in any extended trade and his teamfight presence balloons. So I convert my 6-to-first-item lead: snowball kills, take plates, and end the lane before his soul stacks and item spikes turn him into an unkillable drain tank.
edits.after: You still win the straight 1v1, but Swain is a soul-stacking scaler — full-AP with Liandry's and Rylai's, his R (Demonic Ascension) becomes a near-permanent AoE drain and Rylai's slow makes him sticky enough to land E mid-fight, while Ravenous Flock heals and permanently grows his health bar. Let it go long and he out-sustains your burst in any extended trade. So convert your 6-to-first-item lead: snowball kills, take plates, keep anti-heal up, and end the lane before his soul stacks turn him into a drain tank.

edits.before: Swain owns Levels 1-3 — if his E (Nevermove) root lands he free-casts Q's cone and W's zone, and you have no Shroud yet to escape the follow-up.
edits.after: Swain owns Levels 1-3 — if the return half of his E (Nevermove) roots you he free-casts Q's cone and W's zone, and you have no Shroud yet to escape.

edits.before: Twilight Shroud comes online: sit in the smoke untargetable to dodge his E, then punish his whiffed root with empowered passive ring-autos.
edits.after: Twilight Shroud comes online, but it only breaks his aim: Nevermove roots through smoke and Vision of Empire reveals you — keep moving and punish.

edits.before: His drain + root — build MR, shroud his E. Akali wins the Demonic Ascension cooldown windows.
edits.after: His drain + root — build MR, sidestep the return claw. Akali wins the Nevermove windows.

edits.before: Shroud rewrites any trade he starts. Only take the trade when Swain's Demonic Ascension is down.
edits.after: Smoke breaks his aim, not the wave. Trade when Swain's Nevermove is down, 12s at rank 1.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Poke when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove, 12s at rank 1: matchup-defining — the RETURN claw roots, so sidestep that half. - Vision of Empire reveals you inside Shroud. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: His drain. Poke when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His root, 12s at rank 1. The return half is the one that lands.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Rooted, his Q cone and W zone land free for the whole 12 seconds.

notes: Both layers treated the 120s Demonic Ascension as the tracked lane cooldown; the real one is Nevermove at 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. Two mechanical corrections: Nevermove roots on the return wave, and Vision of Empire (W) is flagged revealsStealth — it strips your Twilight Shroud invisibility. Content 'mid'/'late' were written in first person; converted to the second-person voice.
